To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new technique of constant infusion, indicator-dilution measurement of limb flow was tested and found valid in vitro and in the forelimbs of dogs.

1) a constant infusion, indicator-dilution technique for blood-flow measurements in the forearm or hand of man was validated in vitro and tested in vivo, 2) this technique employs jet injection of indicator to improve mixing of tracer with blood, 3) the jet injection system improved mixing of tracer with arterial blood, and 4) this technique was used to measure limb vascular responses to intrabrachiai-arterial infusions of MgSO4 in normotensive men and

the constant infusion indicator dilution technique, using jet injection to improve arterial mixing, can be used to measure total forearm and hand blood flow and that this technique is useful for studies of the vascular effects of vasoactive agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new constant infusion, indicator technique for measuring blood flow in man and with studies of the forearm and hand vascular response to magnesium infusion.
the measurement of blood flow and vascular reactivity in the limbs of normal and hypertensive man.
the development and validation of a technique that allows accurate measurement of limb blood flows in man, as well as the study of vascular responses of the forearm and hand to vasoactive drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this constant infusion indicator dilution technique provides accurate measurements of blood flow in limbs of man, and the technique has been used to demonstrate a significant difference in forearm vascular response between normotensive and hypertensive men.
the jet injection technique is useful in the study of forearm blood flow in man.
the technique is a useful tool for measuring blood flow in the human limb and that it is a reliable method for measuring the effects of drugs on blood flow in the limb.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the constant infusion, indicator method is reliable and valid for measuring total forearm blood flow.
the constant infusion, indicator-dilution technique with jet injection system for measuring limb blood flow is a reliable technique for use in man.
this method is useful for the study of the forearm vascular bed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to show that this technique is a reliable method for measuring forearm blood flow.
the constant infusion, indicator-dilution technique allows accurate measurement of total limb blood in man.
the jet injection device is useful for mixing substances with arterial blood, especially for substances with high affinity for blood cells.
